Extracellular potassium concentration acutely increases around a neuron.

Transport Mechanisms.caseStem: A 6-year-old child with acute watery diarrhea improves after oral rehydration solution. Pulse, arterial pressure, venous return, and baroreceptor-mediated responses are measured during the first minute after standing. A normal adjacent measurement rules out global failure of the organ system. The measured abnormality is confined to this physiologic step, while upstream stimulation and unrelated adjacent measurements remain intact. The extrinsic coagulation pathway is activated. Which laboratory test is affected first?
Hemostasis.explanation: PT assesses the extrinsic and common pathways, especially factor VII. The correct answer is the finding that most specifically supports the proposed mechanism.
Hemostasis.objective: Interpret coagulation pathway tests. Applied vignette. Focus: confirmatory physiologic finding.

The abnormal variable changes before a downstream compensatory response can account for the finding. The measured abnormality is confined to this physiologic step, while upstream stimulation and unrelated adjacent measurements remain intact. Airway radius decreases during bronchoconstriction. Which effect is expected?
choices: Increased laminar flow at all rates
No change because radius is irrelevant
Respiratory Mechanics.explanation: Airway resistance varies inversely with radius to the fourth power. The correct answer identifies the causal step rather than a downstream association.
Respiratory Mechanics.objective: Apply airway resistance principles. Applied vignette. Focus: cause versus consequence.

V/Q Ratio.caseStem: A 59-year-old man with progressive shortness of breath undergoes pulmonary function and arterial blood gas testing. Airflow, lung volumes, alveolar gas tensions, and oxygen content are measured during a controlled breathing maneuver. The baseline and postintervention measurements are obtained under the same recording conditions. Alveolar gas values change according to the balance between ventilation reaching the unit and blood flow perfusing it. An alveolus is ventilated but not perfused.
V/Q Ratio.stem: A 59-year-old man with progressive shortness of breath undergoes pulmonary function and arterial blood gas testing. Airflow, lung volumes, alveolar gas tensions, and oxygen content are measured during a controlled breathing maneuver. The baseline and postintervention measurements are obtained under the same recording conditions. Alveolar gas values change according to the balance between ventilation reaching the unit and blood flow perfusing it. An alveolus is ventilated but not perfused. What is the V/Q relationship?
V/Q Ratio.explanation: Ventilation without perfusion is dead space and has very high V/Q. The key is the expected direction of change produced by the mechanism.
V/Q Ratio.objective: Identify dead space physiology. Applied vignette. Focus: directional prediction.

In an upright lung, perfusion increases more from apex to base than ventilation does.

The filtration variable changes according to hydrostatic pressure, oncotic pressure, and arteriolar resistance at the glomerulus. Tubular obstruction increases hydrostatic pressure in Bowman space. The finding is present at the site where the relevant transporter, channel, receptor, enzyme, or contractile protein is active. Solute loss exceeds water loss, lowering ECF osmolality so water shifts into cells despite ECF contraction. Primary adrenal insufficiency causes renal sodium chloride wasting with water retention relative to solute. Which pattern is expected after equilibration?

Decreased ECF volume, increased ICF volume, and decreased osmolality
Increased ECF volume with unchanged osmolality
Decreased ECF and ICF volumes with increased osmolality
Increased ECF volume and decreased ICF volume
Body Volume.explanation: Hypotonic contraction removes more solute than water from the ECF, lowering osmolality and shifting water into cells. ECF volume falls, ICF volume rises, and plasma proteins and hematocrit tend to increase. The mechanism explains how the system compensates for the initiating disturbance.

Serum sodium, plasma osmolality, ECF volume, ICF volume, and hematocrit are measured. The dose-response relationship changes in the direction predicted by the altered physiologic step. Solute loss exceeds water loss, lowering ECF osmolality so water shifts into cells despite ECF contraction. Primary adrenal insufficiency causes renal sodium chloride wasting with water retention relative to solute. Which pattern is expected after equilibration?

Decreased ECF volume, increased ICF volume, and decreased osmolality
Increased ECF volume with unchanged osmolality
Decreased ECF and ICF volumes with increased osmolality
Increased ECF volume and decreased ICF volume
Body Volume.explanation: Hypotonic contraction removes more solute than water from the ECF, lowering osmolality and shifting water into cells. ECF volume falls, ICF volume rises, and plasma proteins and hematocrit tend to increase. The correct answer matches the specific site and direction, whereas the alternatives reflect related pathways.
Body Volume.objective: Predict body-fluid changes during hypotonic contraction. Applied vignette. Focus: physiologic discrimination between similar pathways.

The measured abnormality is confined to this physiologic step, while upstream stimulation and unrelated adjacent measurements remain intact. Exercise increases CO2 production, heat production, and oxygen demand.
Multisystem Homeostasis.stem: A 41-year-old patient with prolonged fasting has serial measurements of glucose, ketones, insulin, glucagon, sympathetic tone, and renal acid excretion. The finding is reproduced when the same pathway is challenged by a smaller physiologic stimulus. The measured abnormality is confined to this physiologic step, while upstream stimulation and unrelated adjacent measurements remain intact. Exercise increases CO2 production, heat production, and oxygen demand. Which integrated response is expected?
choices: Increased ventilation, cardiac output, and heat dissipation
Multisystem Homeostasis.explanation: Exercise requires coordinated respiratory, cardiovascular, and thermoregulatory responses. The correct answer describes the physiologic change expected as the system returns toward baseline.
Multisystem Homeostasis.objective: Integrate physiologic responses to exercise. Applied vignette. Focus: recovery physiology.

Multisystem Homeostasis.caseStem: A 41-year-old patient with prolonged fasting has serial measurements of glucose, ketones, insulin, glucagon, sympathetic tone, and renal acid excretion. The finding is reproduced when the same pathway is challenged by a smaller physiologic stimulus. A fall in effective arterial pressure decreases stretch-sensitive afferent firing and increases sympathetic outflow. Acute blood loss reduces arterial pressure.
Multisystem Homeostasis.leadIn: Which rapid compensatory mechanism occurs first?
Multisystem Homeostasis.stem: A 41-year-old patient with prolonged fasting has serial measurements of glucose, ketones, insulin, glucagon, sympathetic tone, and renal acid excretion. A fall in effective arterial pressure decreases stretch-sensitive afferent firing and increases sympathetic outflow. Acute blood loss reduces arterial pressure. Which rapid compensatory mechanism occurs first?
Multisystem Homeostasis.explanation: The baroreflex rapidly increases sympathetic tone after blood pressure falls. The correct answer describes the physiologic change expected as the system returns toward baseline.
Multisystem Homeostasis.objective: Identify rapid compensation for hemorrhage. Applied vignette. Focus: recovery physiology.

Multisystem Homeostasis.caseStem: A patient develops symptoms during a supervised fast. Plasma glucose, insulin, glucagon, ketones, and counterregulatory hormone responses are measured at the time of symptoms. The finding is reproduced when the same pathway is challenged by a smaller physiologic stimulus. The hormone response is interpreted from the direction of feedback between the endocrine signal and its target-organ effect. A patient has prolonged fasting.
Multisystem Homeostasis.stem: A patient develops symptoms during a supervised fast. Plasma glucose, insulin, glucagon, ketones, and counterregulatory hormone responses are measured at the time of symptoms. The finding is reproduced when the same pathway is challenged by a smaller physiologic stimulus. The hormone response is interpreted from the direction of feedback between the endocrine signal and its target-organ effect. A patient has prolonged fasting. Which multisystem pattern is expected?
choices: Low insulin, high glucagon, lipolysis, and ketogenesis
Multisystem Homeostasis.explanation: Fasting shifts metabolism toward hepatic glucose production, lipolysis, and ketone production. The correct answer describes the physiologic change expected as the system returns toward baseline.
Multisystem Homeostasis.objective: Integrate endocrine and metabolic fasting responses. Applied vignette. Focus: recovery physiology.

Multisystem Homeostasis.caseStem: A patient with abnormal thirst and urine volume has plasma osmolality, ADH activity, collecting duct water permeability, and urine osmolality measured during a water deprivation study. The direction of the paired variable is used to identify the primary mechanism rather than a secondary association. A fall in effective arterial pressure decreases stretch-sensitive afferent firing and increases sympathetic outflow. Severe dehydration decreases effective arterial blood volume.
Multisystem Homeostasis.stem: A patient with abnormal thirst and urine volume has plasma osmolality, ADH activity, collecting duct water permeability, and urine osmolality measured during a water deprivation study. The direction of the paired variable is used to identify the primary mechanism rather than a secondary association. A fall in effective arterial pressure decreases stretch-sensitive afferent firing and increases sympathetic outflow. Severe dehydration decreases effective arterial blood volume. Which combined response is expected?
choices: Increased sympathetic tone, RAAS, and ADH
Multisystem Homeostasis.explanation: Volume depletion activates sympathetic tone, RAAS, ADH, and thirst. The correct answer explains why the measured variables move in different directions or magnitudes.
Multisystem Homeostasis.objective: Integrate responses to hypovolemia. Applied vignette. Focus: discordant-variable interpretation.
